overview: Kuk in the New Guinea highlands preserves a long archaeological record of cultivation. It is evidence for changing agricultural practices, not a named kingdom or a single culture with an established lifespan.

items.text: Cultivators propagated bananas, taro and yams vegetatively. The evidence supports independent agricultural development in the region.
Cultivation moved from mounds along wetland margins to drainage through ditches dug with wooden tools.
Successive drainage and cultivation features record deliberate changes to wetland conditions rather than simple dependence on an unmodified landscape.
The archaeological sequence is persistent but episodic. Contemporary farming continues aspects of earlier practices, without proving one unchanging community across the entire sequence.
